steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Point: Your vocabulary choices directly affect your AO6 mark (up to 16 marks). A wide, ambitious vocabulary demonstrates control and precision - but only when used appropriately. | Connotation Matters: "Cheap" and "inexpensive" have similar meanings but different connotations. "Cheap" suggests poor quality; "inexpensive" suggests good value. Choose the word with the right emotional shade. | Common Repeat Offenders: said, went, looked, got, nice, good, thing, something, very, really | Warning: Don't use words you don't fully understand. Misused ambitious vocabulary is worse than correctly used simple vocabulary.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Replace "very happy" with a single, more precise word. | What is the difference in connotation between "cheap" and "inexpensive"? | Rewrite "She walked slowly across the room" using a powerful verb instead of walked + slowly.

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Key Point, Connotation Matters, Common Repeat Offenders, and one past-paper question.
